speaker: Doctor
text: I understand there is a significant concern regarding your fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. To determine the cause, which could range from infection to malignancy, please tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those "drenching night sweats" and twelve pounds of weight loss in just four weeks are very alarming; have you noticed any cough, shortness of breath, or fever recently? Also, please tell me if you have had any recent travel to areas where tuberculosis is common or any known exposure to someone with an active infection.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a "fixed" and enlarged supraclavicular node is highly concerning for malignancy, particularly given your rapid weight loss. To narrow this down, have you noticed any loss of appetite, early satiety, or changes in bowel habits? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, LDH, ESR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC - Elevated, Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased, Platelets - Normal; Lactate_Dehydrogenase - Elevated; ESR - Not Reported

speaker: Doctor
text: The laboratory results showing elevated WBC, anemia, and significantly elevated LDH are consistent with a high-grade lymphoproliferative disorder. Given your supraclavicular node, B-symptoms, and anemia, please tell me if you have noticed any easy bruising, bleeding gums, or a feeling of fullness after eating only a small amount of food? Also, do you have a history of alcohol use disorder or smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sensation of fullness and clothes feeling tighter suggests hepatosplenomegaly, which combined with your supraclavicular node and high LDH strongly points to a lymphoma. Do you have any history of alcohol use or smoking? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Imaging, Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Examination: Slight abdominal distension, dullness noted over the left lower quadrant, splenomegaly detected; Liver_Function_Tests: Not Reported

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of B-symptoms, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, anemia, elevated LDH, and confirmed splenomegaly is highly indicative of a high-grade lymphoproliferative disorder.
